**Finding submitted: deviation (critical) — Article XIII, ¶p0130.**

- **What the document does:** The only cap protects Licensor alone and is set at "one half of the amount paid by the Licensee" — below even a 6-month fee equivalent. The consequential-damages exclusion in (a) also runs one way, and Licensee remains uncapped while carrying a broad one-way indemnity (Article XII, ¶p0128) with no super-cap. No carve-outs for confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
- **Why it fails:** This is walk-away territory under LOL-CAP (customer uncapped / vendor capped; vendor cap under 6 months' fees; indemnities with no super-cap), not merely short of the fallback.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** Two minimal edits inside the existing sentences — mutualise the damages exclusion, and replace clause (b) with a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, plus an "Excluded Claims" carve-out sentence and confirmation that our fee obligations are not capped damages. Fallback offered in the comment is a straight mutual 12-month fee cap with the core carve-outs.
